about: Structural corrections to the vendored Summa (sources/summa/summa.xml, CCEL) from R7, read by 1.7. Keys are the source's own paragraph ids (2.1's Summa anchors are the article div id plus this id's suffix, e.g. FP_Q76_A3-p4 is summa/FP_Q76_A3/p4). Each entry gives the Leonine role and number of the paragraph's unit, its reply targets ('obj N', 'sc N'), any move to another article, and flags. 'targets' is set on a paragraph that is a reply; 'also_answers' on a paragraph of another part that also carries a reply sentence; 'holds' on a paragraph that carries further Latin units of its part (a second sed contra). 'class' is R7's verdict: prose-reply, joint-reply, variant, source-error or omission; 'defect' says whose it is, 'ccel' when the printed edition is right and the CCEL text is wrong, 'translators' when the print has it too. 'latin' cites the Leonine unit by its Corpus Thomisticum unit number; 'printed' cites the printed English edition (keys in 'print'). IDs, numbers and short labels only: no passage text. Recovered text goes in a separate vendored override file, never here. See docs/research/R7-summa-structure.md.
latin_source: Leonine edition (Rome, from 1888) as published by Corpus Thomisticum (https://www.corpusthomisticum.org/iopera.html), 87 pages, fetched 30 Oct 2026; unit numbers are Corpus Thomisticum's
